newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end higher on cold weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end higher on cold weather concerns.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled firmer amid concerns of cold weather moving into Florida over the next two weeks, traders and analysts said.

"There is a one in six chance of a cold front next week and into the following week in the citrus area of Florida," said analyst Judy Ganes of Merrill Lynch. "It's causing some nervousness in the market and a little shortcovering."
Most-active March orange juice settled 1.50 cents firmer at 96.00 cents per pound. Spot January went out 1.65 cents higher at 92.40 cents.
Smith Barney weatherman Jon Davis said there was no threat of significant cold weather in Florida's citrus belt through next Thursday.
"After that, the situation has to be watched very closely," he said. Next Friday and Saturday the first of numerous Arctic airmasses moves down into central and eastern U.S.
"At this time it does not look like a major damage threat but it is close enough to keep an extremely close eye on the situation," Davis said.
Merrill Lynch said in its Citrus Weekly Letter that Florida's crop was late, with only 23.6 million gallons of FCOJ processed so far compared to 43 million a year ago.
"Sources indicate that some Brazilian shipments are scheduled to arrive in the next few weeks which could also weigh on the market, again assuming no frost," Merrill Lynch said.
"With record production anticipated, imports will need to drop from year ago comparisons to prevent a build-up in supplies, especially if movement is lagging," Merrill said.
